newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK BANK IRB RAISES PRIME RATE - JAN 20.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK BANK IRB RAISES PRIME RATE - JAN 20.

text.p: Investicna a Rozvojova Banka (IRB) a.s., Slovakia's third largest commercial bank, on Thursday said it was raising its prime rate lending to 13.5 percent from a previous 12.5 percent, effective January 20.
The move comes as interbank money market rates remain high due to a liquidity crunch affecting almost the entire banking sector.

The sector has become highly illiquid since the central bank stopped quoting securities repo and reverse repo rates at the beginning of the year, instead holding tenders when needed for limited volumes of short-term securities repos.
Rates on the money market currently range between 20-26 percent.
The bank said in a statement it was also raising its interest rates on time and demand crown deposits up to six months by 20-30 basis points.
The statement did not include any comment on the moves.
